newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia rate cut due to slow economy - Opp'n.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia rate cut due to slow economy - Opp'n.

text.p: Australian opposition treasury spokesman Gareth Evans said the Reserve Bank's interest rate cut was a reaction to the sluggishness of the Australian economy.
"The truth of the matter is that the Australian economy has been sharply deteriorating," Evans told reporters after the RBA cut interest rates on Wednesday.
"It desperately needed a stimulus," Evans said.
"I just hope that this half a percent will be enough."
The Reserve Bank earlier eased monetary policy, dropping its overnight cash rate target to 6.5 percent from 7.0 percent.
Evans said there may be room for further rate cuts by the end of the year, or early in 1997.
"I think we just have to wait and see at the moment what the impact of this half a percent will be on confidence and expectations," Evans said.
"We were looking for a significant cut on this occasion and we got it with half a percent," he said.
"Maybe there was room for more, maybe there will be room for more before the end of the year, or certainly early in the new year," Evans said.
